name: FL-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+14 PVI) in an open seat
Republican Schwartzel has vastly outraised the Democratic nominee
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The seat sits in a heavily Republican-leaning district, and the Republican nominee has raised roughly $2.1 million against under $60,000 for the Democrat, while markets price the race at 94% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic spending or outside support could narrow the margin, but the district's lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving the seat to run for governor, making this an open contest in a southwest Florida district that leans about fourteen points Republican. Jim Schwartzel enters as the Republican nominee with a large financial advantage, having raised over $2 million, while Democrat Victor Arias has raised under $60,000 and has no outside support on record. An independent candidate trails far behind in both money and visibility.

Prediction markets give the Republican about a 94% chance of holding the seat, and no public general-election polls or expert ratings are available to suggest otherwise. The fundamentals point to a Republican hold in the mid-teens, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
